gold.label: R-100
gold.text:
- **R-100 (vocabulary).** The system is a factory. Its stages are unit operations; each declares
  inputs, outputs, an operating envelope (rate, ceiling, thresholds in the control file) and its
  gates. Valves are control-file switches that open or close a unit operation for a graph. Products
  are graphs of declared type. "Pipeline" is retired as the name of the system; the `pipeline`
  module keeps its name as the DAG executor, because renaming code is churn.

gold.label: R-101
gold.text:
- **R-101 (one integrated run, per graph, never a central service).** `squiddy build <graph>`
  runs the unit-operation DAG end to end as one long-running, resumable, rate-limited,
  progress-tracked process: checkpoint per unit, resume by skip, metered spend against the graph's
  ceiling and bucket, a status view, and a STOP file. It pauses only at the closed list of operator
  touchpoints (L4: spend above the standing band, an external send or publication, a value input
  the system is designed to measure, an incident notice). Each graph instantiates its own factory
  floor from the kit; there is no central runtime holding content (the Wintermute monolith lesson
  stands, CLAUDE.md "never runs as a service" is unchanged: a per-graph daemon is not a service).

gold.label: R-102
gold.text:
- **R-102 (the human is at the walls).** Inputs the human owns: the purpose statement of the graph
  (what it exists to answer, as a class), what documents go in and what searches are run to find
  more, the spend band, the publication decision. Outputs the human consumes: the served surface,
  through an LLM over MCP. Inside the walls, no human check exists and none is designed (DI-098,
  DI-131). Quality loops are instruments with positive and negative controls (methodology 7.6).
  Competency questions are generated by the machine from the purpose statement and the corpus,
  judged by a calibrated model judge; the human may add questions and never gates on them. This is
  how Q-003 already ran: Gemini wrote the 24 questions, Fable judged, the probe gate calibrated the
  judge. The one human act in that round (the paste) was removed by ADDENDUM 07.

gold.label: R-103
gold.text:
- **R-103 (statistical quality control on every unit operation).** Every unit operation carries
  pre-registered gates, planted controls that prove each gate fires (X-001), metered spend, and a
  kill rule whose firing stops the line and opens an assignable-cause investigation before anything
  restarts. Q-004 is the template for that investigation. Floors are set before data and moved only
  by a logged correction to a pre-registered rule (DN-021), never after the fact.

gold.label: R-104
gold.text:
- **R-104 (products differ; fundamentals do not).** The invariant core every graph gets from the
  kit: the identity spine, the event-sourced ledger with the store as a rebuildable projection,
  grounding spans located at birth, the administrative layer (OpenAlex or the domain's authority),
  entity resolution with recoverable merges, drift and parity gates, conformance gates with
  controls, versioned releases, and one MCP surface generated from the graph's schema. The product
  type (policy graph, evidence graph, readiness graph, exercise-science graph) is a schema, a
  recipe and a gate configuration, never new machinery. Whether the surfaces should converge on a
  universal connector contract is tabled at the operator's word.

gold.label: R-105
gold.text:
- **R-105 (continuous maintenance is a product function).** Scheduled unit operations, never
  unbounded agents: admission of a new document (one file, one command, minutes, extraction shown
  before commit); supersession and retirement by logged events (built); currency sweeps;
  measure-before-commit re-extraction when a better model appears (DI-026); and refutation, which
  is new: when later evidence contradicts a recorded claim, the contradiction is a logged
  adjudication attached to both claims, never a deletion (DI-044). Refutation is a research problem
  with prior art (SciFact and its successors) and gets its own pre-registered design before it is
  built.

gold.label: R-106
gold.text:
- **R-106 (the served surface is decided by evidence per graph).** What a product serves is the
  outcome of that graph's own downstream test, run as a unit operation with a valve, before bulk
  spend (X-001 item 18). A claims layer is served where it beats the baseline on the graph's own
  questions; where it does not, metadata plus full text plus concepts is the product and claims
  are an overlay the surface may cite. The factory therefore builds the cheap layers first and
  earns the expensive ones.

gold.label: R-115
gold.text:
- **R-115 (the unit-operation DAG, per graph).** `squiddy build --graph <dir>` runs this DAG. Each
  node is a unit operation the kit already has; the edges are the data each consumes. Valves are
  control-file switches (R-117) named in brackets.

gold.label: R-125
gold.text:
- **R-125 (the population of the checkpoint bar).** Constitution section 15 binds every loop the
  factory RUNS and every maintenance unit; it does not bind a frozen instrument whose registered
  numbers came from it, because rewriting the instrument changes the instrument. The bar is
  restated as: every loop a factory node or maintenance unit executes is checkpointed (six
  properties), and every other loop in the repository is named in a register with one of three
  dispositions: `factory` (bound), `frozen_instrument` (exempt, with the Results it produced), or
  `to_fix` (bound when next touched). The register lives in `squiddy/loops.yaml` and the static
  check reads it; an unregistered loop fails the check. `admit_batch` write and `currency.sweep`
  are `to_fix`.

gold.label: R-126
gold.text:
- **R-126 (the demand gate is read by release binding, never updated in place).** A verdict is a
  Result named `<gate>` bound to a release (item 20). The valve reads the verdict bound to the
  release the graph currently serves; an older verdict for an older release stays in the register
  untouched. No Result is updated; a second run on the same release is refused (the test is bound
  to its release) unless the control file carries a dated re-test line, as Q-005 ADDENDUM 01 did.

gold.label: R-127
gold.text:
- **R-127 (the 1,185 are an input-wall decision until their origin is known).** Which documents
  go in is the operator's (R-102). Before any of them is assessed, acquired or admitted, the
  factory reports what they are: which task cataloged them, of what kind, how many the graph's
  own criterion would admit, and the acquisition cost at the declared buckets. That report is a
  `plan` output of the factory (`squiddy build plan --graph library`), zero calls. The assess node
  on a graph with entries the operator has not seen reported is a touchpoint 3 pause, once, with
  the report; the control file line that clears it names the count and the date.

gold.label: R-128
gold.text:
- **R-128 (DN-026 corrected, and biblio's index inputs).** The four inaccuracies in section 1 are
  corrected here, not by editing DN-026 (design notes are records). The R-115 drawing's `parse`
  position is corrected: parse follows write. The index node takes its metadata documents from the
  graph's emit spec (R-123); this is ordered as an F-001 addendum step, with biblio's `index:
  not_applicable` unchanged until a graph that indexes needs it, which is Arnold.

gold.label: R-129
gold.text:
- **R-129 (the input is a scope statement in the operator's words).** The block is renamed
  `scope:`. Required: `topic`, a paragraph in the operator's words naming the collection he wants
  (exercise science and martial arts; federal AI readiness; the KG-construction literature).
  Optional: `anchors`, sources, ideas or phrases he already knows the graph must cover;
  `exclusions`, what it must not become (the AI-washing case). No field asks for questions, a
  class of questions, or intended uses. `init` requires only `topic`. R-102's "what it exists to
  answer, as a class" and R-121 item 3's wording are amended to this; touchpoint 3 is the scope
  statement and anything the operator later adds to it.

gold.label: R-130
gold.text:
- **R-130 (competency questions are the machine's instrument).** The `questions` node generates
  them from the corpus plus the scope statement (the Rebboud/Alharbi line, as Q-001 ADDENDUM 02
  already ran); they test the build against the pre-registered bar and never specify it. The
  operator may add questions and never gates on a verdict (R-102, unchanged). `anchors` become a
  coverage gate at release, not questions: every anchor resolves to at least one located receipt
  through the served verbs, with a planted missing anchor as the positive control.

gold.label: R-131
gold.text:
- **R-131 (the question set grows with use).** The served surface logs every query it answers
  (verb, arguments, receipts returned, timestamp) to `<graph>/factory/queries.jsonl`, local to the
  graph, never shipped, controlled by `serve.log_queries` in the control file (required key,
  default in the template `true`). The maintenance-time demand test draws its questions from that
  log plus a fresh generated set, so utility is measured on what was actually asked and the
  instrument follows the exploration (Bates 1989). A query is data, never an instruction to the
  factory.

gold.label: R-132
gold.text:
- **R-132 ("throw a video against the literature" is a verb).** `check(text or transcript)`:
  segment the input, `search` each segment, return the located receipts that support or
  contradict it, with `claims_in` as the overlay where a claims layer exists. It is the front door
  of the refutation unit (R-105) and is recorded here as a product verb candidate for Arnold,
  built after refutation's own design note; the intake side is the existing `ingest-youtube`
  skill. Not part of F-001.

gold.label: R-135
gold.text:
- **R-135 (the maintenance loop is demonstrated as one run, with every event of record).** On the
  served library graph, through the factory's maintenance entries, in this order: admit one new
  document the operator did not choose (the machine picks a work cited by the corpus and not held,
  from the administrative layer); supersede one held preprint by its published expression (an
  HV-004 pair); run the currency sweep; cut the release; run the anchors and index-parity gates;
  serve; touch STOP mid-run once and resume. Every step is a ledger event; the status view is
  captured at each step; the served surface answers a query on the new document afterwards. The
  demand test is not re-run (it is bound to its release and costs about 464k tokens; R-126's dated
  re-test line is the operator's if he wants it).

gold.label: R-137
gold.text:
- **R-137 (decisions and acquisition answers are inputs of a build).** The input wall carries
  three things, not one: the intake, the graph's decision record (the manifest's decided entries
  with their reasons and provenance) and the acquisition record (K-002's records log, imported
  once as keyed records of the factory's acquire node). A build that receives a decision record
  applies it before the graph's criterion: a decided entry is not undecided, and only entries the
  record does not cover reach R-127's pause. So a rebuild of a served graph pauses at nothing
  (M-001 A.2 holds for rebuilds) and a first build of a new graph pauses once, by design, with
  the plan report (R-127 holds for first builds). Resolver answers are read from the acquisition
  record by unit key; a request leaves the machine only for an entry the record does not hold.

gold.label: R-138
gold.text:
- **R-138 (every served layer is produced by a node; the census is the coverage gate).** Each
  class in a served graph's census names the factory node that produces it, in the graph's emit
  spec. A class with no producing node fails a conformance gate (no orphan layer), with a planted
  orphan as the control. Under this rule library's DAG gains: `resolve` (HV-003/HV-004 identity
  merges, before write); text attachment inside `acquire` (HV-005, which today runs as
  `tools/attach_texts.py`); `admin` as both a build node and a maintenance unit M-06 for Works in
  the pending slice; `concepts` (HV-006's scan) under a valve of its own, zero model calls; a
  second intake source for standards, since `catalog` takes N sources. Claim stays the extract
  valve's.

gold.label: R-139
gold.text:
- **R-139 (identifier lookups bind to the registration agency).** When an entry is cataloged from
  an identifier, the title, authors and container of record are the registration agency's
  (Crossref, DataCite, arXiv for its own ids); an aggregator's `display_name` is a hint and is
  recorded beside it as `title_aggregator`. A similarity below the gate's threshold between the
  two is an `authority_conflict` event, and the entry is cataloged under the registered title.
  The M-001 pick is corrected by this rule as a maintenance event, not re-admitted.

gold.label: R-140
gold.text:
- **R-140 (currency findings feed a repair unit, M-07).** For each id the sweep reports not
  current: a DOI that fails ISO 26324 syntax is stripped, and the expression is re-resolved by
  title and authors through the registration agencies; a syntactically valid DOI answering 404 is
  re-queried once at the agency and once at OpenAlex, then recorded `unresolved` with the date; an
  OpenAlex work id that no longer resolves is re-resolved by DOI. Every outcome is a ledger event
  on the expression; an expression that ends with no valid identifier keeps its text and its
  citation string and loses only the key. X-001 item 16's key gate extends to Expression DOIs.

gold.label: R-142
gold.text:
- **R-142 (network policy is per process and deny-by-default).** Every process the factory
  starts, and `squiddy serve`, runs under a declared network policy: `none` or a list of HTTP
  buckets. `none` is enforced two ways at once: `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`/`ALL_PROXY` set to a
  closed local port with `NO_PROXY` empty, and on macOS a `sandbox-exec` profile denying network,
  when the kit can apply it. A node with buckets gets the real network for those hosts only
  (the proxy is the call layer's own allowlisting forwarder). `serve` is `none` always.

gold.label: R-143
gold.text:

  the ML stack, and every entry point (`serve`, `index`, `arms`, `concepts`, tools) imports the
  kit first. A module that imports `transformers`, `sentence_transformers` or `huggingface_hub`
  before the kit fails a test.

gold.label: R-144
gold.text:
- **R-144 (the egress check is dynamic; the static check is kept, not trusted alone).** The suite
  gains an egress tier: every entry point and every node whose policy is `none` is started under
  R-142's closed network on the fixture graph and must succeed; a planted library-level call (a
  stub module that opens a socket at import) must fail it. The static check stays for kit source.
  No "offline" or "no network" claim appears in a docstring, spec or report without naming the
  egress test that proves it.

gold.text:
